sourceDate.text: 大慕容夫人生樂平戾王丕

units.zh: 明元皇帝七男。
units.en: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons.
units.literal: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons.

units.zh: 杜密皇后生世祖太武皇帝。
units.en: Empress Mi of the Du clan bore Shizu Emperor Taiwu.
units.literal: Empress Mi of the Du clan gave birth to Shizu Emperor Taiwu.

units.zh: 大慕容夫人生樂平戾王丕。
units.en: Lady Da Murong bore Prince Pi of Leping, who received the posthumous title Ill-Fated King.
units.literal: Lady Da Murong gave birth to Prince Pi of Leping, posthumously styled the Ill-Fated King.

units.zh: 安定殤王彌闕母氏。
units.en: Prince Mi of Anding, posthumously styled the Early-Deceased King, is of unknown maternity.
units.literal: Prince Mi of Anding, posthumously styled the Early-Deceased King — his mother's name is not recorded.

units.zh: 慕容夫人生樂安宣王範。
units.en: Lady Murong bore Prince Fan of Le'an, who received the posthumous title Proclaiming King.
units.literal: Lady Murong gave birth to Prince Fan of Le'an, posthumously styled the Proclaiming King.

units.zh: 尹夫人生永昌莊王健。
units.en: Lady Yin bore Prince Jian of Yongchang, who received the posthumous title Magnificent King.
units.literal: Lady Yin gave birth to Prince Jian of Yongchang, posthumously styled the Magnificent King.

units.zh: 建寧王崇、新興王俊二王，並闕母氏。
units.en: The Princes Chong of Jianning and Jun of Xinxing both have unrecorded mothers.
units.literal: The two princes, Chong of Jianning and Jun of Xinxing, both lack recorded mothers.

units.zh: 樂平王丕，少有才幹，為世所稱。
units.en: Pi, Prince of Leping, had talent and ability from youth and was praised by his generation.
units.literal: Pi, Prince of Leping, had talent and ability from youth and was praised by his generation.

units.zh: 太宗以丕長，愛其器度，特優異之。
units.en: Because Pi was the eldest, Taizong admired his bearing and treated him with special favor.
units.literal: Because Pi was the eldest, Taizong admired his bearing and treated him with special favor.

units.zh: 泰常七年封，拜車騎大將軍。
units.en: In the seventh year of Taichang he was enfeoffed and appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Taichang he was enfeoffed and appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

units.zh: 後督河西、高平諸軍討南秦王楊難當，軍至略陽，禁令齊肅，所過無私，百姓爭致牛酒。
units.en: Later he commanded the armies of Hexi and Gaoping against Yang Nandang, Prince of Southern Qin. When the army reached Lueyang, discipline was strict and orderly; wherever it passed there was no private plunder, and the people competed to bring cattle and wine.
units.literal: Later he commanded the armies of Hexi and Gaoping against Yang Nandang, Prince of Southern Qin. When the army reached Lueyang, discipline was strict and orderly; wherever it passed there was no private plunder, and the people competed to bring cattle and wine.

units.zh: 難當懼，還仇池。
units.en: Nandang was afraid and returned to Chouchi.
units.literal: Nandang was afraid and returned to Chouchi.

units.zh: 而諸將議曰，若不誅豪帥，軍還之後，必聚而為寇。
units.en: The generals argued, "If we do not execute the powerful leaders, then after the army returns they will surely gather and become bandits."
units.literal: The generals argued, "If we do not execute the powerful leaders, then after the army returns they will surely gather and become bandits."

units.zh: 又以大眾遠出，不有所掠，則無以充軍實，賞將士。
units.en: They also reasoned that since the great army had come far, if nothing were seized there would be no way to fill the army stores and reward the soldiers.
units.literal: They also reasoned that since the great army had come far, if nothing were seized there would be no way to fill the army stores and reward the soldiers.

units.zh: 將從之。
units.en: Pi was about to follow this advice.
units.literal: Pi was about to follow this advice.

units.zh: 時中書侍郎高允參丕軍事，諫曰：「今若誅之，是傷其向化之心，恐大軍一還，為亂必速。」
units.en: At the time Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun was participating in Pi's military affairs. He remonstrated, "If we execute them now, this will wound their will to submit to transformation. I fear that once the great army returns, rebellion will come quickly."
units.literal: At the time Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun was participating in Pi's military affairs. He remonstrated, "If we execute them now, this will wound their will to submit to transformation. I fear that once the great army returns, rebellion will come quickly."

units.zh: 丕以為然，於是綏懷初附，秋毫無犯。
units.en: Pi considered this right, and so he soothed and embraced those newly attached, without violating so much as an autumn hair.
units.literal: Pi considered this right, and so he soothed and embraced those newly attached, without violating so much as an autumn hair.

units.zh: 初，馮弘之奔高麗，世祖詔遣送之，高麗不遣，世祖怒，將討之。
units.en: Earlier, when Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo, Shizu ordered that he be sent back. Goguryeo did not send him, and Shizu was angry and intended to attack.
units.literal: Earlier, when Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo, Shizu ordered that he be sent back. Goguryeo did not send him, and Shizu was angry and intended to attack.

units.zh: 丕上疏，以為和龍新定，宜優復之，使廣修農殖，以饒軍實，然後進圖，可一舉而滅。
units.en: Pi submitted a memorial arguing that Helong had only recently been pacified and should be generously relieved so that farming and planting could be widely restored and military supplies made abundant; only afterward should plans advance, when Goguryeo could be destroyed in one stroke.
units.literal: Pi submitted a memorial arguing that Helong had only recently been pacified and should be generously relieved so that farming and planting could be widely restored and military supplies made abundant; only afterward should plans advance, when Goguryeo could be destroyed in one stroke.

units.zh: 帝納之，乃止。
units.en: The emperor accepted this and stopped.
units.literal: The emperor accepted this and stopped.

units.zh: 後坐劉潔事，以憂薨。
units.en: Later, implicated in Liu Jie's affair, Pi died of anxiety.
units.literal: Later, implicated in Liu Jie's affair, Pi died of anxiety.

units.zh: 事在
units.en: The affair is recorded
units.literal: The affair is recorded

units.zh: 〈潔傳〉。
units.en: in Jie's biography.
units.literal: in Jie's biography.

units.zh: 諡曰戾王。
units.en: His posthumous title was Prince Li.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Prince Li.

units.zh: 子拔，襲爵。
units.en: His son Ba inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Ba succeeded to the title.

units.zh: 後坐事賜死，國除。
units.en: Later he was condemned for a crime and ordered to take his own life, and the fief was abolished.
units.literal: Later, because of an offense, he was ordered to commit suicide, and the fief was extinguished.

units.zh: 丕之薨及日者董道秀之死也，高允遂著筮論曰：「昔明元末起白臺，其高二十餘丈，樂平王嘗夢登其上，四望無所見。
units.en: When Prince Pi died and the diviner Dong Daoxiu was put to death, Gao Yun wrote a treatise on divination, saying: "Near the end of Emperor Mingyuan's reign a White Terrace was built, more than twenty zhang tall. The Prince of Leping once dreamed that he climbed it and gazed in every direction, yet saw nothing at all.
units.literal: At the death of Pi and the execution of the diviner Dong Daoxiu, Gao Yun thereupon composed a treatise on divination, saying: "In the late reign of Emperor Mingyuan a White Terrace was erected, more than twenty zhang in height. The Prince of Leping once dreamed of climbing it and looking in all four directions, yet saw nothing.

units.zh: 王以問日者董道秀，筮之曰：『大吉。』
units.en: The prince consulted the diviner Dong Daoxiu, who cast the hexagram and declared, 'Great good fortune.'
units.literal: The prince asked the diviner Dong Daoxiu about it; Dong divined and said: 'Great good fortune.'

units.zh: 王默而有喜色。
units.en: The prince said nothing, yet his face showed delight.
units.literal: The prince was silent but showed a pleased expression.

units.zh: 後事發，王遂憂死，而道秀棄市。
units.en: When the matter later came to light, the prince died of anxiety, and Daoxiu was executed in the public marketplace.
units.literal: Later the affair came to light; the prince died of grief, and Daoxiu was executed in the marketplace.

units.zh: 道秀若推六爻以對王曰：『易稱「亢龍有悔」，窮高曰亢，高而無民，不為善也。』
units.en: Had Daoxiu worked through the six lines and answered the prince, saying, 'The Changes says, "The arrogant dragon will have cause for regret." To press height to the limit is arrogance; to stand aloft without the people beneath one is no blessing,'
units.literal: If Daoxiu had analyzed the six lines and replied to the prince, saying: 'The Changes states, "The arrogant dragon will have cause for regret." To reach the extreme of height is called arrogance; to stand high yet without the people is not good.'

units.zh: 夫如是，則上寧於王，下保於己，福祿方至，豈有禍哉？
units.en: then above he would have reassured the prince, and below he would have kept himself safe; fortune and rank would have followed — how could calamity have come of it?
units.literal: If it had been so, then above he would have secured the prince's peace, and below he would have preserved himself — blessing and emolument would then arrive; how could there have been disaster?

units.zh: 今舍於本而從其末，咎釁之至不亦宜乎！」
units.en: But as it was, he abandoned the root and clung to the branch — was it not only fitting that guilt and disaster should overtake them?"
units.literal: Now, having abandoned the root to follow the branch, was it not fitting that blame and calamity should arrive!"

units.zh: 安定王彌，泰常七年封。
units.en: Prince Mi of Anding was enfeoffed in the seventh year of the Taichang era.
units.literal: Prince Mi of Anding was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

units.zh: 太宗討滑臺，留守京師。
units.en: When Emperor Taizong marched against Huatai, he stayed behind to guard the capital.
units.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Huatai, he remained to guard the capital.

units.zh: 薨，諡殤王。
units.en: He died and was given the posthumous title Early-Deceased King.
units.literal: He died and was posthumously styled the Early-Deceased King.

units.zh: 無子，國除。
units.en: He left no sons, and the fief was abolished.
units.literal: He had no sons, and the fief was extinguished.

units.zh: 樂安王範，泰常七年封。
units.en: Fan, Prince of Le'an, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.
units.literal: Fan, Prince of Le'an, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

units.zh: 雅性沉厚，寬和仁恕。
units.en: His natural character was deep and generous, broad, mild, humane, and forgiving.
units.literal: His natural character was deep and generous, broad, mild, humane, and forgiving.

units.zh: 世祖以長安形勝之地，非範莫可任者，乃拜範都督五州諸軍事、衞大將軍、開府儀同三司、長安鎮都大將，高選才能，以為僚佐。
units.en: Shizu considered Chang'an a strategically commanding place and believed no one but Fan could be entrusted with it. He therefore appointed Fan commander of military affairs in five provinces, Grand General of the Guards, with an opened office and protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and grand general of Chang'an Garrison, selecting able men of high quality to serve as his staff.
units.literal: Shizu considered Chang'an a strategically commanding place and believed no one but Fan could be entrusted with it. He therefore appointed Fan commander of military affairs in five provinces, Grand General of the Guards, with an opened office and protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and grand general of Chang'an Garrison, selecting able men of high quality to serve as his staff.

units.zh: 範謙恭惠下，推心撫納，百姓稱之。
units.en: Fan was modest and respectful, kind to those below him, and received and soothed people with open sincerity; the common people praised him.
units.literal: Fan was modest and respectful, kind to those below him, and received and soothed people with open sincerity; the common people praised him.

units.zh: 時秦土新罹寇賊，流亡者相繼，範請崇易簡之治，帝納之。
units.en: At the time the Qin lands had newly suffered bandits and rebels, and refugees followed one after another. Fan requested that rule there honor ease and simplicity, and the emperor accepted it.
units.literal: At the time the Qin lands had newly suffered bandits and rebels, and refugees followed one after another. Fan requested that rule there honor ease and simplicity, and the emperor accepted it.

units.zh: 於是遂寬徭，與人休息。
units.en: Thereupon corvée was relaxed, and the people were allowed to rest.
units.literal: Thereupon corvée was relaxed, and the people were allowed to rest.

units.zh: 後劉潔之謀，範聞而不告。
units.en: Later, when Liu Jie plotted, Fan heard of it but did not report it.
units.literal: Later, when Liu Jie plotted, Fan heard of it but did not report it.

units.zh: 事發，因疾暴薨。
units.en: When the affair came to light, he suddenly died from illness.
units.literal: When the affair came to light, he suddenly died from illness.

units.zh: 長子良。
units.en: His eldest son was Liang.
units.literal: His eldest son was Liang.

units.zh: 世祖未有子，嘗曰：「兄弟之子猶子也。」
units.en: Shizu had not yet fathered a son and once said, "A brother's son is as good as one's own."
units.literal: Shizu had no son yet and once said: "A brother's son is like one's own son."

units.zh: 親撫養之。
units.en: He raised Liang himself with fatherly care.
units.literal: He personally reared and nurtured him.

units.zh: 長而壯勇多知，常參軍國大計。
units.en: When he came of age he was strong, courageous, and well informed, and he regularly joined in deliberations on matters of state and war.
units.literal: When grown, he was bold, brave, and deeply informed, and he regularly took part in great plans of state and army.

units.zh: 高宗時，襲王。
units.en: Under Emperor Gaozong he inherited the princedom.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozong, he inherited the princedom.

units.zh: 拜長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史，為內都大官。
units.en: He was appointed Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison, Inspector of Yong Province, and Director of the Inner Capital.
units.literal: He was appointed Grand General of the Capital Garrison of Chang'an and Inspector of Yong Province, and served as Director of the Inner Capital.

units.zh: 薨，諡曰簡王。
units.en: He died and was given the posthumous title Simple King.
units.literal: He died and was posthumously styled the Simple King.

units.zh: 永昌王健，泰常七年封。
units.en: Jian, Prince of Yongchang, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.
units.literal: Jian, Prince of Yongchang, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

units.zh: 健姿貌魁壯，善弓馬，達兵法，所在征戰，常有大功。
units.en: Jian was imposing and robust in appearance, skilled with bow and horse, and expert in military methods; wherever he campaigned, he regularly won great merit.
units.literal: Jian was imposing and robust in appearance, skilled with bow and horse, and expert in military methods; wherever he campaigned, he regularly won great merit.

units.zh: 才藝比陳留桓王，而智略過之。
units.en: In talent and skill he was comparable to Prince Huan of Chenliu, while in wisdom and strategy he surpassed him.
units.literal: In talent and skill he was comparable to Prince Huan of Chenliu, while in wisdom and strategy he surpassed him.

units.zh: 從世祖破赫連昌，遂西略至木根山。
units.en: He followed Shizu in defeating Helian Chang and then campaigned west as far as Mugen Mountain.
units.literal: He followed Shizu in defeating Helian Chang and then campaigned west as far as Mugen Mountain.

units.zh: 討和龍，健別攻拔建德。
units.en: During the campaign against Helong, Jian separately attacked and took Jiande.
units.literal: During the campaign against Helong, Jian separately attacked and took Jiande.

units.zh: 後平叛胡白龍餘黨于西河。
units.en: Later he pacified the remaining followers of the rebel Hu Bailong in Xihe.
units.literal: Later he pacified the remaining followers of the rebel Hu Bailong in Xihe.

units.zh: 世祖襲蠕蠕，越涿邪山。
units.en: When Shizu made a surprise attack on the Rouran, he crossed Zhuoxie Mountain.
units.literal: When Shizu made a surprise attack on the Rouran, he crossed Zhuoxie Mountain.

units.zh: 車駕還，詔健殿後，蠕蠕萬騎追之，健與數十騎擊之，矢不虛發，所中皆應弦而斃，遂退。
units.en: As the imperial carriage returned, an edict ordered Jian to guard the rear. Ten thousand Rouran cavalry pursued, and Jian struck them with several dozen riders. Not one arrow was loosed in vain; whoever he hit fell dead at the string, and the pursuers withdrew.
units.literal: As the imperial carriage returned, an edict ordered Jian to guard the rear. Ten thousand Rouran cavalry pursued, and Jian struck them with several dozen riders. Not one arrow was loosed in vain; whoever he hit fell dead at the string, and the pursuers withdrew.

units.zh: 威震漠北。
units.en: His awe shook the north of the desert.
units.literal: His awe shook the north of the desert.

units.zh: 尋從平涼州，健功居多。
units.en: Soon afterward he followed in pacifying Liangzhou, and Jian's merit was the greatest.
units.literal: Soon afterward he followed in pacifying Liangzhou, and Jian's merit was the greatest.

units.zh: 又討破禿髮保周，自殺，傳首京師；
units.en: He also attacked and defeated Tufa Baozhou, who killed himself, and Jian sent his head to the capital;
units.literal: He also attacked and defeated Tufa Baozhou, who killed himself, and Jian sent his head to the capital;

units.zh: 復降沮渠無諱。
units.en: he then brought Juqu Wuhui to surrender.
units.literal: he then brought Juqu Wuhui to surrender.

units.zh: 無疾薨，諡曰莊王。
units.en: He died without illness and received the posthumous title Prince Zhuang.
units.literal: He died without illness and received the posthumous title Prince Zhuang.

units.zh: 子仁，襲。
units.en: His son Ren inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Ren succeeded.

units.zh: 仁亦驍勇，有父風，世祖奇之。
units.en: Ren was likewise fierce and brave, with his father's bearing, and Shizu took special notice of him.
units.literal: Ren was also fierce and valiant, having his father's manner; Shizu regarded him with wonder.

units.zh: 後與濮陽王閭若文謀為不軌，發覺，賜死，國除。
units.en: Later he conspired in treason with Lü Ruowen, Prince of Puyang; when the plot was uncovered he was ordered to take his own life, and the fief was abolished.
units.literal: Later he plotted treason with Prince Ruowen of Puyang, Lü Ruowen; when discovered, he was ordered to commit suicide, and the fief was extinguished.

units.zh: 建寧王崇，泰常七年封，拜輔國將軍。
units.en: Prince Chong of Jianning was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang and appointed General Who Assists the State.
units.literal: Prince Chong of Jianning was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang and appointed General Who Assists the State.

units.zh: 從討北虜有功。
units.en: He took part in campaigns against the northern foes and won distinction.
units.literal: He followed in campaigns against the northern barbarians and achieved merit.

units.zh: 高宗時，封崇子麗濟南王。
units.en: Under Emperor Gaozong, Chong's son Li was enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozong, Chong's son Li was enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.

units.zh: 後與京兆王杜元寶謀逆，父子並賜死。
units.en: Later he plotted rebellion with Du Yuanbao, Prince of Jingzhao; father and son were both ordered to take their own lives.
units.literal: Later he plotted rebellion with Prince Yuanbao of Jingzhao, Du Yuanbao; father and son were both ordered to commit suicide.

units.zh: 新興王俊，泰常七年封，拜鎮東大將軍。
units.en: Prince Jun of Xinxing was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang and appointed Grand General Who Guards the East.
units.literal: Prince Jun of Xinxing was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang and appointed Grand General Who Guards the East.

units.zh: 少善騎射，多才藝。
units.en: From boyhood he excelled at riding and archery and had many accomplishments.
units.literal: From youth he was skilled at horsemanship and archery and possessed many talents.

units.zh: 坐法，削爵為公。
units.en: Convicted under the law, he was stripped of his princely rank and reduced to duke.
units.literal: Because of a legal offense, his nobility was reduced and he was made a duke.

units.zh: 俊好酒色，多越法度。
units.en: Jun was devoted to wine and women and often overstepped the bounds of law.
units.literal: Jun was fond of wine and women and often transgressed the laws.

units.zh: 又以母先遇罪死，而己被貶削，恒懷怨望，頗有悖心。
units.en: His mother had earlier been condemned and executed, and he himself had been demoted and stripped of rank; he nursed a lasting grievance and came to harbor rebellious intent.
units.literal: Moreover, because his mother had previously been condemned and put to death while he himself had been demoted and stripped of rank, he constantly harbored resentment and bore a rebellious heart.

units.zh: 後事發，賜死，國除。
units.en: When the matter later came to light he was ordered to take his own life, and the fief was abolished.
units.literal: Later the affair came to light; he was ordered to commit suicide, and the fief was extinguished.

units.zh: 論曰：樂平、樂安俱以將領自效，竟以憂迫而逝，驗克終之為鮮。
units.en: The appraisal says: Leping and Le'an both proved themselves as commanders, yet in the end died under anxiety and pressure, showing how rare it is to come to a good end.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Leping and Le'an both proved themselves as commanders, yet in the end died under anxiety and pressure, showing how rare it is to come to a good end.

units.zh: 莊王才力智謀，一時之傑，與夫建寧、新興，不同日也。
units.en: Prince Zhuang, in talent, strength, wisdom, and strategy, was an outstanding man of his age; he cannot be spoken of in the same breath as Jianning and Xinxing.
units.literal: Prince Zhuang, in talent, strength, wisdom, and strategy, was an outstanding man of his age; he cannot be spoken of in the same breath as Jianning and Xinxing.

units.zh: 校勘記
units.en: Collation Notes
units.literal: Collation Notes

units.zh: 魏書卷十七 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，百衲本、汲本、局本卷末有宋人校語云：「魏收書明元六王列傳亡。」
units.en: The tables of contents in various editions of the Book of Wei mark this volume as deficient. At the end of the Baibaina, Ji, and Ju editions a Song-dynasty collation note reads: "Wei Shou's original biography of Emperor Mingyuan's six princes is lost."
units.literal: In the table of contents of various editions of the Book of Wei, volume 17 is marked "deficient." At the end of the Baibaina, Ji, and Ju editions, a Song-dynasty collation note states: "Wei Shou's original biography of Emperor Mingyuan's six princes is lost."

units.zh: 殿本考證云：「魏收書亡，後人所補。」
units.en: The Dian edition's textual verification states: "Wei Shou's text is lost; this was supplied by later hands."
units.literal: The Dian edition's textual verification states: "Wei Shou's text is lost; later men supplied this."

units.zh: 按此卷以北史卷一六明元六王傳補，間有溢出字句，當出於高氏小史。
units.en: This volume was restored from the biography of Emperor Mingyuan's six princes in juan 16 of the History of the Northern Dynasties; occasional stray phrases appear that likely come from the Xiaoshi compiled by the Gao family.
units.literal: This volume was supplemented from the biography of Emperor Mingyuan's six princes in juan 16 of the History of the Northern Dynasties; here and there are superfluous characters and phrases, which likely derive from the Xiaoshi of the Gao clan.

units.zh: 以太子少傅魏收為兼尚書右僕射。
units.en: Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Wei Shou was made Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince Wei Shou was appointed Concurrent Right Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 己卯，兼右僕射魏收以阿縱除名。
units.en: On the jimao day, Concurrent Right Vice Director Wei Shou was dismissed from office for fawning and indulgence.
units.literal: On the jimao day, Concurrent Right Deputy Director Wei Shou was dismissed from office for fawning and indulgence.

units.zh: 世祖之克赫連昌，詔雲與常山王素留鎮統萬。
units.en: When Shizu took Helian Chang, he ordered Yun and Prince Su of Changshan to hold Tongwan.
units.literal: When Shizu captured Helian Chang, he issued an edict Yun and the Prince of Changshan Su to remain and garrison Tongwan.

units.zh: 元孝友，祖魏太武皇帝。
units.en: Yuan Xiaoyou — his grandfather was Emperor Taiwu of Wei.
units.literal: Yuan Xiaoyou — his grandfather was Emperor Taiwu of Wei.

units.zh: 元坦 元斌 元孝友 元暉業 元弼 元韶
units.en: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao
units.literal: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao

units.zh: 國史自鄧淵、崔琛、崔浩、高允、李彪、崔光以還，諸人相繼撰錄，綦儁及偉等諂說上黨王天穆及尒朱世隆，以為國書正應代人修緝，不宜委之餘人，是以儁、偉等更主大籍。
units.en: Since Deng Yuan, Cui Chen, Cui Hao, Gao Yun, Li Biao, and Cui Guang, the national history had been compiled in turn by successive scholars; Qi Jun, Wei, and others flattered Shangdang Prince Tianmu and Erzhu Shilong, arguing that the state annals ought to be edited by men of Dai and not entrusted to outsiders—so Jun, Wei, and their circle again took charge of the great registers.
units.literal: The national histories, from Deng Yuan, Cui Chen, Cui Hao, Gao Yun, Li Biao, Cui Guang onward, were written in succession by various men; Qi Jun and Wei and others flattered Shangdang Wang Tianmu and Erzhu Shilong, saying that the national book ought properly to be compiled by men of Dai and should not be entrusted to others—thus Jun, Wei, and the others again took charge of the great registers.

units.zh: 氐王楊難當從兄子文德聚衆茄蘆，宋世加以爵位。
units.en: Wende, a cousin's son of the Di king Yang Nandang, gathered forces at Jialu and received titles under the Song.
units.literal: The Di king Yang Nan-dang's cousin's son Wende gathered a host at Jialu; in the Song era titles and ranks were added to him.

units.zh: 難當族弟廣香先奔虜，元徽中，爲虜攻殺文慶，以爲陰平公、茄蘆鎮主。
units.en: Nandang's younger clansman-brother Guangxiang had earlier fled to the Northern Wei; in the Yuanhui era he attacked and killed Wenqing for them and was made Duke of Yinping and commander of Jialu.
units.literal: Nandang's clansman younger brother Guangxiang first fled to the barbarians; in the Yuanhui era he attacked and killed Wenqing for the barbarians and was made Duke of Yinping and chief of Jialu garrison.

units.zh: 後鮮卑馮弘稱燕王，治黃龍城，託跋燾伐之，脩之與同沒人邢懷明並從。
units.en: Later the Xianbei Feng Hong declared himself King of Yan and ruled from Huanglongcheng. When Tuoba Tao marched against him, Xiuzhi followed with fellow captive Xing Huaiming.
units.literal: Later the Xianbei Feng Hong styled himself King of Yan and ruled from Huanglongcheng. Tuoba Tao attacked him, and Xiuzhi went along with fellow captive Xing Huaiming.

units.zh: 時魏屢伐弘，或說弘遣脩之歸求救，遂遣之。
units.en: Wei was then attacking Hong repeatedly. Some advised Hong to send Xiuzhi south to beg Song for rescue, and Hong dispatched him.
units.literal: At that time Wei repeatedly attacked Hong. Some urged Hong to send Xiuzhi back to seek Song aid, and he sent him off.

units.zh: 脩之、懷明懼奔馮弘，弘不禮。
units.en: Fearing for their lives, Xiuzhi and Huaiming fled to Feng Hong, who showed them no honor.
units.literal: Xiuzhi and Huaiming, in fear, fled to Feng Hong, who did not treat them with courtesy.

units.zh: 尚書劉潔、武京侯安原請先平馮跋。
units.en: Liu Jie of the Masters of Writing and An Yuan, Marquis of Wujing, urged that Feng Bo be subdued first.
units.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie and Marquis of Wujing An Yuan asked to pacify Feng Bo first.

units.zh: 尚書劉潔武京侯安原請先平馮跋 卷三０安原傳「武京」作「武原」。
units.en: Minister Liu Jie, Marquis of Wujing, Hou Anyuan, and others asked to pacify Feng Bo first: juan 30, Anyuan's life, has "Wujing" as "Wuyuan."
units.literal: Minister of Writing Liu Jie, Marquis of Wujing, Hou Anyuan, and others asked to pacify Feng Bo first. Juan 30, Anyuan biography, reads "Wujing" as "Wuyuan."

units.zh: 世祖討山胡白龍，意甚輕之，單將數十騎登山臨嶮，每日如此。
units.en: When Emperor Shizu campaigned against the Mountain Hu chieftain Bai Long, he took the enemy lightly and would ride up alone with only a few dozen horsemen to overlook the steep passes, doing so day after day.
units.literal: Emperor Shizu campaigned against the Mountain Hu Bai Long and thought it quite light; alone he led several dozen horsemen up the mountain overlooking the defile, daily so.

units.zh: 白龍乃伏壯士十餘處，出於不意，世祖墮馬，幾至不測。
units.en: Bai Long had hidden stalwart warriors in more than ten places; they sprang out unexpectedly, the emperor was thrown from his horse, and he came within a hair's breadth of disaster.
units.literal: Bai Long then hid stalwart warriors in more than ten places, emerging unexpectedly; Emperor Shizu fell from his horse and nearly reached beyond reckoning.

units.zh: 太宗在東宮，給事帳下，侍從遊獵，夙夜無怠。
units.en: While Emperor Taizong was still heir in the Eastern Palace, Luoer served in his personal staff, accompanying him on the hunt by day and night without slackening.
units.literal: When Taizong was in the Eastern Palace, he served in the tent staff, attending hunts, never idle from dawn to night.

units.zh: 太宗即位，拜散騎常侍。
units.en: After Emperor Taizong acceded to the throne, Luoer was appointed Regular Attendant.
units.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 太宗嘗獵于灅南，乘冰而濟，冰陷沒馬，洛兒投水，奉太宗出岸。
units.en: Once when Emperor Taizong was hunting at Shuainan and crossed a river on the ice, the ice broke and his horse went under; Luoer plunged into the water and brought the emperor safely to shore.
units.literal: Taizong once hunted at Shuainan, crossing on ice; the ice gave way and submerged the horse; Luoer threw himself into the water and bore Taizong out to the bank.

units.zh: 水沒洛兒，殆將凍死，太宗解衣以賜之。
units.en: The water closed over Luoer and he was nearly frozen to death; the emperor stripped off his own garment and gave it to him.
units.literal: The water submerged Luoer and he nearly froze to death; Taizong removed his coat to grant him.

units.zh: 天賜末，太宗出居于外，洛兒晨夜侍衞，無須臾違離，恭勤發於至誠。
units.en: Near the end of the Tiansi reign, when Emperor Taizong was forced to live outside the palace, Luoer guarded him morning and night without leaving his side for an instant, his reverent service springing from the deepest loyalty.
units.literal: At the end of Tiansi, Taizong went out to dwell elsewhere; Luoer attended day and night without a moment's departure, diligence born of utmost sincerity.

units.zh: 元紹之逆，太宗左右唯洛兒與車路頭而已。
units.en: During Yuan Shao's revolt, of all those close to Emperor Taizong only Luoer and Che Lutou remained.
units.literal: During Yuan Shao's rebellion, of Taizong's close attendants there were only Luoer and Che Lutou.

units.zh: 太宗還宮，社稷獲乂，洛兒有功焉。
units.en: When Emperor Taizong returned to the palace and the realm was restored to order, Luoer had earned a share of the credit.
units.literal: Taizong returned to the palace; the altars of state were settled; Luoer had merit therein.

units.zh: 太宗親臨哀慟者數四焉。
units.en: Emperor Taizong came in person to mourn him, weeping again and again.
units.literal: Taizong in person came to mourn, weeping several times.

units.zh: 少以忠厚選給東宮，為太宗帳下帥。
units.en: In his youth he was chosen for the Eastern Palace on account of his honesty and loyalty and became commander of Emperor Taizong's personal guard.
units.literal: In youth, for his honesty and kindness he was selected to serve the Eastern Palace as Tent Commander under Taizong.

units.zh: 天賜末，太宗出於外，路頭隨侍竭力。
units.en: Near the end of the Tiansi reign, when Emperor Taizong was forced out of the palace, Lutou followed and served him with all his strength.
units.literal: At the end of Tiansi, Taizong lived outside; Lutou followed and served with all his strength.

units.zh: 及太宗即位，拜為散騎常侍，賜爵金鄉公，加忠意將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Taizong acceded, Lutou was appointed Regular Attendant, enfeoffed as Duke of Jinxiang, and made General of Loyal Intent.
units.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Regular Attendant, granted the title Duke of Jinxiang, added General of Loyal Intent.

units.zh: 太宗性明察，羣臣多以職事遇譴，至有杖罰，故路頭優遊不任事，侍宿左右，從容談笑而已。
units.en: Emperor Taizong was keen and exacting; many officials were punished for faults in their duties, some even beaten with the staff, so Lutou held no active post and merely kept night watch at the emperor's side, passing the time in easy talk and laughter.
units.literal: Taizong's nature was sharp in perception; many officials were punished for their duties, even to beating; therefore Lutou leisurely did not take office, staying by his side at night, merely conversing and laughing at ease.

units.zh: 太宗亦敬納之，寵待隆厚，賞賜無數，當時功臣親幸莫及。
units.en: Emperor Taizong likewise respected and heeded him; his favor was lavish and his gifts beyond counting, and among the meritorious ministers of the day none enjoyed such intimacy.
units.literal: Taizong also respected and accepted this; favor was thick, rewards countless; among meritorious officials of the time none matched his intimacy.

units.zh: 太宗親臨哀慟。
units.en: Emperor Taizong came in person to mourn him.
units.literal: Taizong in person came to mourn.

units.zh: 太宗時，選為直郎。
units.en: During Emperor Taizong's reign he was chosen as a direct attendant.
units.literal: In Taizong's time he was selected as Direct Gentleman.

units.zh: 按卷三太宗紀永興三年十二月甲午見「任城公嵇拔」，泰常四年甲戌，記「獻懷長公主子嵇敬封長樂王」，與此傳合。
units.en: Juan 3 of the Taizong Annals, twelfth month of Yongxing year 3 (day jiawu), records "Duke of Rencheng Ji Ba," and Taichang year 4 (day jiaxu) records "Ji Jing, son of the Elder Princess of Xianhuai, enfeoffed as Prince of Changle," which agrees with this biography.
units.literal: Examining: juan 3 Taizong Annals, twelfth month of Yongxing year 3, day jiawu, records "Duke of Rencheng Ji Ba"; Taichang year 4, day jiaxu, records "Son of the Elder Princess of Xianhuai Ji Jing enfeoffed as Prince of Changle" — matching this biography.

units.zh: 高宗即位，典選部、主客二曹。
units.en: After Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, Tong oversaw the Selection and Host and Guest bureaus.
units.literal: When Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, he managed the two bureaus of Selection and Host and Guest.

units.zh: 高宗初，賜爵阜城侯，加冠軍將軍。
units.en: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fucheng and appointed Champion General.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign, he was granted the title Marquis of Fucheng, added Champion General.

units.zh: 高宗以建貪暴懦弱，遣使就州罰杖五十。
units.en: Because Jian was greedy, cruel, and weak in character, Emperor Gaozong sent an envoy to his province to have him beaten with fifty strokes of the staff.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozong because Jian was greedy, brutal and weak, sent a messenger to the prefecture to punish with fifty cane strokes.

younger brother by the same mother
en:younger brother of the former king of hejian
younger brother of the former King of Hejian
